annotation.title_clean: THE ETHICS OF ROBOTS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
annotation.title_en: The Ethics of Robots and Artificial Intelligence
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Petrikat, D.; Chan, P.; Hosein, N.
annotation.venue: Journal of Applied Business and Economics (JABE)
annotation.summary_en: Journal article examining public perception of the ethics of robots and AI, framed through the Industrial Revolution and Luddite history. The excerpt stresses job-loss fears (25-40% of jobs) and how public attitudes will affect organizations' and governments' use of the technology. It proposes no specific governance mechanisms.
key_provisions_or_claims: Public perception of robot and AI ethics shapes how effectively organizations and governments can use the technology.
Robots, automation and AI continue the Industrial Revolution's transformation of society.
Predicted 25-40% job loss from AI and automation fuels worker resistance, as with the Luddites.
Reactions to technology depend on culture and on economic, social and political context.
